host_samples.sample_event: Linux software CPU clock, user-mode instruction pointer + thread ID, 997 Hz per attached thread; QMP query-cpus-fast maps vCPU threads. Attach after process launch, stop after UART completion and QMP stop. These samples include guest startup and output copying, not host-side post-run comparisons. Time asleep or descheduled is excluded.
host_samples.native_fmaf_evidence: Matching executable and debug symbols; QEMU float32_muladd calls fmaf@plt at 0x8397bc. PLT entry 0x45d2f0. Host libm fmaf IFUNC resolves to 0x42960: endbr64, vfmadd213ss, ret. Ranges [0x45d2f0,0x45d300) and [0x42960,0x4296a) verified by disassembly.
limits: FMA category includes dispatch and floating-point semantics; it does not measure pure hardware FMA latency.
The memory category covers only positively identified address lookup/memory helpers; loads, stores and inline address checks in anonymous JIT code cannot be split by these IP samples.
Direct translation is a conservative classification. Anonymous executable and nonidentified functions are not silently assigned to translation or floating point.
CPU sample shares are not elapsed-time shares or an estimate of achievable wall speedup.

marginal_first.method: One warmup and eight rotated/reversed trials. Both whole-score-dispatch timers are outside the K loop. Matched scalar RV64 assembly keeps registers, addresses, accumulation order, checks and output. The two extra-work arms add duplicate hot loads or same-operand FMAs to a scratch register. Deltas are marginal times, not additive shares of original execution; no cold-cache or DRAM attribution.

marginal_repeat.method: One warmup and eight rotated/reversed trials on the same inputs. Guest counters bracket the dispatch outside the K loop. Extra hot loads or duplicate FMAs discard their results in a scratch register. Paired differences measure marginal cost with this access pattern.

copy_repeat.metric: median forward_s: QEMU start to UART; no guest instrumentation
